newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan opposition leader concedes defeat in poll.
newsitem.headline: Japan opposition leader concedes defeat in poll.

text.p: The head of Japan's main opposition party, Ichiro Ozawa, conceded defeat for his group after Sunday's general elections.
"The results of the elections show that we fell far short of our goal of reaching a majority," Ozawa told a televised news conference. "We regret this very much."
His Shinshinto (New Frontier Party) had been projected to win some 156 seats in parliament's 500-seat Lower House. It held 160 seats in the old Lower House.
"Our policies, despite our efforts to make them very clear, were not understood by the electorate. But we respect the will of the people," Ozawa said.
He refused to say whether he would step down as party leader. "The party leadership will thoroughly review all aspects of the election, including the party leadership itself."
Ozawa had declared that his party was aiming to win nothing less than a majority of the contested seats.
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) was projected to win some 240 seats, short of an overall majority.
Shinshinto was formed from nine parties in December 1994.
